title: dedicated-throughput-regression-hypothesis-and-sleuthing
content:
Summary:

Quick notes from the night shift investigating a progressive throughput/latency regression in a Dedicated GPU pool (pool-id: dp-17). The symptom was a widening tail-latency distribution for small (<1s baseline) generation requests between 02:30–05:00 UTC, accompanied by periodic evictions and a drop in effective concurrent QPS. Preliminary signal: autoscaler churn + allocator affinity change -> KV-cache churn -> longer cold-path token generation.

What we saw (high level):
- Sudden step-up in 95p/99p token-latency around 02:30 UTC, repeated every ~12–18 minutes for ~2h.
- Autoscaler created and removed 2–3 nodes in short succession during each oscillation.
- Tenant-level failures: one largest tenant (tenant-A) saw transient OOM-like alloc failures and feed-forward requeues.
- KV-cache hit-rate dropped from ~92% to ~40% on impacted hosts during episodes.

Detection signals used:
- pool_latency_95p, pool_latency_99p (console: /dashboards/pools/dp-17/latency)
- allocator_eviction_rate
- node_startup_time and node_termination_count
- per-tenant cache_hit_ratio (sampler: 1s)
- autoscaler_event_stream (kinesis)

Timeline (compressed):
- 02:28 UTC: first latency spike; autoscaler triggers scale-up (min_size set to 0, config: cooldown 60s, scale_factor 1.8)
- 02:29–02:31: new node join; allocator rebalances tenants; KV-cache prefetched entries invalidated due to partial restart ordering
- 02:32: eviction cascade: allocator marks a host for eviction due to noisy-tenant affinity rule, movers reassign sessions -> additional cache misses
- 02:40: autoscaler decides to scale down (cooldown misaligned), kills a warm host -> additional cold starts
- 02:45–04:30: repeated oscillation at ~12–18m intervals while traffic pattern included bursts from tenant-A and intermittent background evaluation jobs

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler cooldown and responsiveness too aggressive for short bursty workload; scale-up then immediate scale-down causes churn, causing cache thrash and higher tail latency.
2) Allocator affinity regression: a recent rollout changed tenant packing rules so noisy tenants are allowed to be spread across more hosts, increasing surface area for cache invalidation.
3) KV-cache eviction policy combined with startup ordering causes majority of requests hitting cold path when nodes join/leave.
4) Background evaluation job from tenant-A caused memory pressure and local swaps, amplifying eviction decisions.

Quick experiments run during incident (notes):
- Temporarily set autoscaler.min_size=2 for dp-17 at 03:05 UTC -> reduced oscillation amplitude, latency stabilized within 10 minutes. (reverted 04:10 per rollback plan)
- Pinned tenant-A to the same host-group via temporary allocation hint at 03:22 UTC -> KV-cache hit-rate for that tenant recovered to ~86% and their tail latency improved.
- Increased autoscaler.cooldown from 60s to 300s on a staging copy to validate sustained-burst handling (results: fewer joins/leaves but slower sustained scale-up).

Immediate mitigations we applied:
- Manual override: set autoscaler.min_size=2 and cooldown=180s for dp-17 (03:10 UTC) to stop churn.
- Added temporary allocator constraint to favor tenant co-location where safe (03:25 UTC).
- Temporarily suspended background eval job from tenant-A (03:40 UTC) after confirming it's non-critical.

What we learned (post-incident synthesis):
- Short cooldowns are dangerous with KV-cache-heavy workloads; join/leave ordering matters more than we thought.
- Tenant-affinity heuristics are fragile: a small packing change allowed a noisy tenant to be spread across hosts, multiplying cache invalidations.
- Autoscaler decisions must incorporate cache-warmth signals (cache_hit_ratio) and not just CPU/GPU utilization.

Draft runbook additions (actions & playbook snippets)
- Add a circuit-breaker rule to the autoscaler: if pool_latency_95p increases > 30% and recent_node_joins>1 in last 5m, extend cooldown to 10m and set min_size at current_capacity.
- Introduce a cache-warmth probe: before scaling down, ensure per-host cache_hit_ratio > 70% or host_age > X minutes.
- Emergency operator commands (to be codified into CLI):
  - embargo-churn --pool dp-17 --min-size 2 --cooldown 300   # stop autoscaler churn
  - allocator-pin-tenant --tenant tenant-A --group g-3 --ttl 2h
  - suspend-job --tenant tenant-A --job-id eval-1982
- Dashboard shortcuts to include in runbook: link to pool dp-17 latency, node join stream, per-tenant cache heatmap.

Longer term follow-ups (owners & rough ETA):
- eng-serving-runtime: add cache-warmth telemetry into autoscaler decision surface (owner: Lin Zhao, ETA: 3w)
- eng-platform: revert recent packing rule in allocator and add rollout guard (owner: Omar Rodriguez, ETA: 2w)
- product/solutions: notify large tenants about evaluation job scheduling (owner: Drew Kaplan, ETA: 1w)
- SRE: automate the temporary override commands into a safer operator action with audit logging (owner: Maya Patel, ETA: 1w)

Open questions we still have:
- How many other pools/runs use the same background evaluation pattern? Are we rolling this pattern into other customers unknowingly?
- Is there a cheaper pre-warm strategy for KV cache (persistent prefill across restarts)?
- Should autoscaler consider a predictive scaling window fed by short-term workload forecasting?

On-call notes (free-form, timestamped):
- 02:35: noticed 99p jump via phone alert; hit console -> saw node churn.
- 02:50: attempted autoscaler tweak (min=1 -> no effect), rolled back.
- 03:05: changed min_size=2; immediate partial improvement.
- 03:22: tried tenant pin; major recovery for tenant-A but not pool-wide.
- 03:40: suspended tenant-A eval job; cleanest reduction in background noise.

Postmortem checklist items (to include in final incident report):
- Root cause hypothesis verification via blameless experiment logs (compare host-level cache timelines before/after pinning)
- Reproduce in staging with synthetic bursty traffic and background eval jobs
- Config guardrails for autoscaler cooldowns based on pool profile
- Longer-term: implement cache-aware scaling and allocator rollout safety checks

Appendix: useful commands & traces (operators should copy/paste)
- list recent node joins: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" https://infra-api.internal/pools/dp-17/nodes?since=2024-11-15T02:00:00Z
- run temporary pin: ssh ops@allocatorctl "allocator-pin-tenant --tenant tenant-A --group g-3 --ttl 120"
- fetch cache heatmap: kubectl exec -n serving dp-17-cache-proxy -- /usr/local/bin/cache-status --json | jq '.'

Notes to the postmortem author: please keep this doc as the working draft. Save final incident report to Confluence and link here. I tried to keep command snippets low-risk but validate in staging before running in production.
